name: Mascot Agent
summary: The agent as a quiet teal character born from the logo’s dot, peeking over your dashboard and pointing at the anomaly with its eyes.
look: Soft teal-to-peach paper, white product cards, and a round teal mascot with two white oval eyes that squashes, stretches and acts only with its eyes; dotted gaze lines connect it to what matters.

components.name: Mascot body
components.role: teal ellipse with a soft top-left highlight; distinct from the logo — no face is ever added to the mark

components.name: Eye kit
components.role: neutral · focus (narrow) · alarm (wide) · happy (arcs) · blink — the only expressions

components.name: Squash & stretch
components.role: ±16 % from the base, volume preserved; landings always on a beat, shadow scales with it

components.name: Gaze line
components.role: dotted arc from the eyes to the target (anomaly cell, CTA)

components.name: Hands
components.role: two small round nubs that appear only when gripping or holding

components.name: Onion skin
components.role: faded previous poses along the path — storyboard only; plays as real motion in production

motion.name: Birth arc
motion.how: dot → body along a bezier over 3 beats (1.5 s at 120 BPM), stretch 1.3 on the way, squash 0.84 on landing, back.out(2)

motion.name: Eye tracking
motion.how: eyes translate ≤ 0.3 r toward the active column, power2.out 0.2 s, one move per beat

motion.name: Blink + hop
motion.how: blink = eye scaleY 1 → 0.1 → 1 in 0.12 s on off-beats; hop = y −40 px + squash in 0.35 s landing on the downbeat

story: Hook: dashboard cards orbit the question on a dashed ring — no mascot, the chaos is human. Reveal: the Acme mark’s dot pulses, a copy stretches along an arc and lands as the mascot, which opens its eyes; the Acme Pulse wordmark sets. Proof: the mascot peeks over the team’s metrics table, eyes tracking checks, until they widen at Checkout conversion −18% (since 09:42, after deploy #2231) and the human gets Roll back / Acknowledge. CTA: the mascot sits beside the lockup and glances at the coral Start free button.
adapt: Derive the character from a shape in your own mark (a dot, a corner, a letter counter) without altering the logo itself, and give it one job: pointing the human to what matters.

references.note: how Duolingo animates its characters with state-driven poses
squash & stretch and the 12 principles of animation

fit.risk: Can feel childish for serious buyers; character animation is costly to do well.
